learning_objective: 🎯 Move beyond basic averages! Learn to measure how spread out or consistent data is using Mean Deviation, Variance, and Standard Deviation.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Averages (Mean, Median, Mode) only tell you the center of the data. Dispersion tells you how scattered or spread out the data is. A class where everyone scores 50 has a mean of 50. A class where half score 0 and half score 100 also has a mean of 50. Dispersion helps us see the difference!

This measures the average absolute distance of every data point from the Mean (or Median). Formula: $M.D. = \frac{\sum |x_i - \bar{x}|}{n}$. We use absolute values $|...|$ because we only care about the distance, not whether it is positive or negative.

Instead of using absolute values, Variance ($\sigma^2$) squares the differences to make them positive: $\sigma^2 = \frac{\sum (x_i - \bar{x})^2}{n}$. The Standard Deviation ($\sigma$) is simply the square root of the Variance. A lower Standard Deviation means the data is more consistent and stable.

If you want to compare the consistency of two completely different sets of data (like Virat Kohli's runs vs. a bowler's wickets taken), you use C.V. Formula: $C.V. = \frac{\sigma}{\bar{x}} \times 100$. The series with the lower C.V. is more consistent/stable.

fun_activity.title: 🏏 The Consistent Batsman Test
fun_activity.instructions: Batsman A scores: 50, 48, 52, 50. Batsman B scores: 0, 100, 10, 90. Both have an average (mean) of 50 runs per match! But calculating the Standard Deviation will immediately show Batsman A's deviation is near 0 (highly consistent), while B's is massive (highly unpredictable). That's why selectors use statistics!

exam_tips: 📌 When calculating Variance, use the shortcut formula: $\sigma^2 = \frac{1}{n} \sum x_i^2 - (\bar{x})^2$. It saves you from calculating the difference for every single point.

📌 Standard Deviation is independent of the choice of origin (adding/subtracting a constant to all data points doesn't change $\sigma$) but it is NOT independent of scale (multiplying all data points by $k$ multiplies $\sigma$ by $|k|$).
📌 Be very careful when applying formulas: Ungrouped data formulas are different from Grouped data (where you must multiply by frequency $f_i$).
quick_recap: ⭐ Range is the simplest measure of dispersion (Maximum value - Minimum value).
⭐ Variance is the square of the Standard Deviation.
⭐ For comparing the variability or consistency of two series, always calculate and compare their Coefficient of Variation (C.V.).
